{{distinguish|Sub-Riemannian manifold}}
[[File:Sphere filled blue.svg|thumb|The [[sphere]] <math>S^n</math> with the round metric is a Riemannian submanifold of <math>\mathbb R^{n+1}</math>.]]

A '''Riemannian submanifold''' <math>N</math> of a [[Riemannian manifold]] <math>M</math> is a [[submanifold]] <math>N</math> of <math>M</math> equipped with the [[Riemannian metric]] inherited ([[induced metric|induced]]) from <math>M</math>.

Specifically, if <math>(M,g)</math> is a Riemannian manifold (with or without boundary) and <math>i : N \to M</math> is an [[immersed submanifold]] or an [[embedded submanifold]] (with or without boundary), the [[Pullback (differential geometry)|pullback]] <math>i^* g</math> of <math>g</math> is a Riemannian metric on <math>N</math>, and <math>(N, i^*g)</math> is said to be a '''Riemannian submanifold''' of <math>(M,g)</math>. On the other hand, if <math>N</math> already has a Riemannian metric <math>\tilde g</math>, then the immersion (or embedding) <math>i : N \to M</math> is called an '''[[isometric immersion]]''' (or '''[[isometric embedding]]''') if <math>\tilde g = i^* g</math>. Hence isometric immersions and isometric embeddings are Riemannian submanifolds.<ref>{{cite book|last=Lee|first=John|title=Introduction to Riemannian Manifolds|year=2018|edition=2nd}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Chen|first=Bang-Yen|title=Geometry of Submanifolds|year=1973|publisher=Mercel Dekker|location=New York|isbn=0-8247-6075-1|pages=298}}</ref>

For example, the [[n-sphere]] <math>S^n = \{ x \in \mathbb R^{n+1} : \lVert x \rVert = 1 \}</math> is an embedded Riemannian submanifold of <math>\mathbb R^{n+1}</math> via the inclusion map <math>S^n \hookrightarrow \mathbb R^{n+1}</math> that takes a point in <math>S^n</math> to the corresponding point in the superset <math>\mathbb R^{n+1}</math>. The induced metric on <math>S^n</math> is called the round metric.
